claims.text: Disorder-induced broadening of the magnetic transition governs the magnetocaloric response of nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy-alloy films or nanoribbons.
Disorder-induced broadening of the magnetic transition governs hysteresis in these low-dimensional alloys.
Magnetoelastic coupling governs the magnetocaloric response of these low-dimensional alloys.
Magnetoelastic coupling governs hysteresis in these low-dimensional alloys.
Applied magnetic field influences magnetoelastic coupling.
Microstructural state can influence the magnetocaloric response of a high-entropy alloy.
The applied magnetic-field change affects magnetocaloric response and refrigerant capacity.
Random chemical disorder can alter lattice behavior.
The interplay between disorder-induced transition broadening and magnetoelastic coupling is the operative mechanism.
Low-field magnetic-cooling cycling will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the stated bulk baseline.
Low-field magnetic-cooling cycling will reduce hysteresis relative to the stated bulk baseline.
The predicted enhancement and hysteresis reduction arise from the combination of disorder and magnetoelastic coupling.
Heat-transfer rate limits the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The low-dimensional state imposes a boundary on the proposed behavior.
Failure to observe both enhanced magnetocaloric response and reduced hysteresis under the specified conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The requested comparison is relative to an as-deposited baseline, but the hypothesis identifies bulk material as the baseline and does not define an untreated or uncycled as-deposited thin-film control. Consequently, the reference for 'enhanced' response and 'reduced' hysteresis is inconsistent or ambiguous.
